academic_translation:
If a mind arises that forsakes the welfare of others,
Desires to pursue my own welfare,
Or desires to speak,
Then I should remain like a log of wood.
translation: If my mind wants to drop the good of others to seek my own good, or if it just wants to speak, then I should stay like a log.

academic_translation:
Impatience, laziness, and fear,
And likewise impudence and idle chatter,
Or if a mind attached to my own side arises,
At that time, I should remain like a log of wood.
translation: When impatience, laziness, and fear appear, along with rudeness and idle talk. Or if a mind attached to my own side comes up, at that time I should stay like a log.

academic_translation:
Having thus examined the mind for complete affliction,
And for its striving for meaningless things,
At that time, the hero, by means of an antidote,
Should firmly hold it.
translation: I must check my mind for any troubling emotion and for chasing meaningless things. At that time, a hero should use a remedy to hold the mind firmly.

academic_translation:
With utmost certainty and excellent faith,
Steadfast, respectful, and courteous,
With a sense of shame and with apprehension,
Be peaceful and strive to make others happy.
translation: With strong certainty and deep trust, I should be steady, respectful, and polite. With a sense of shame and a fear of doing wrong, I should be peaceful and try hard to make others happy.

academic_translation:
Do not be disheartened by the mutually discordant
Desires of childish ones,
But thinking, "Because afflictions have arisen in them,
This mind of theirs has arisen," be a compassionate one.
translation: I should not be upset by the clashing desires of any childish person. Instead, I should think, "This mind of theirs has appeared because a troubling emotion grew in them." I will be a compassionate one.

academic_translation:
Regarding blameless things,
Governed by myself and sentient beings,
Like an emanation, without "I",
I should always hold this mind.
translation: When I do things that are free of blame with myself and any living being, I must always hold my mind like a magical creation. It must not have any 'I' in it.

academic_translation:
After a long time, the supreme leisure,
Reflecting again and again on having obtained it,
Such a mind, like Mount Meru,
I should hold completely unshakable.
translation: It took a long time to get this best chance to practise. I should think about this again and again. I must keep my mind as steady and unshakable as Mount Meru.

academic_translation:
By vultures craving flesh,
Even when the body is dragged back and forth everywhere,
If you, O mind, are not displeased,
Why do you now care for it?
translation: When hungry vultures drag this dead body all around, you are not upset, my mind. So why do you care so much for it right now?

academic_translation:
Having grasped this body as "mine,"
O mind, why do you guard it?
If you and this are separate,
What can it do for you?
translation: My mind, you hold onto this body and call it 'mine'. But why do you guard it so closely? You and the body are completely separate. What can it really do for you?

academic_translation:
Mind of delusion, for what reason
Do you not grasp a clean wooden form?
This machine of a collection of impurities,
What is the use of guarding this rotten thing?
translation: My mind of confusion, why do you not hold onto a clean wooden shape instead? This body is just a machine made of filth. What is the use of guarding this rotten thing?

academic_translation:
First, this layer of skin,
Separate it with your own intellect;
And the flesh from the lattice of bones,
Separate it off with the weapon of wisdom.
translation: First, use your own thinking mind to separate this layer of skin. Then, use the blade of wisdom to separate the flesh from the web of bones.

academic_translation:
Having separated even the bones,
Look down to the marrow,
And examine for yourself,
"What essence is there in this?"
translation: Take apart even the bones. Look right down to the marrow. Check for yourself. What essence is really in there?

academic_translation:
If, having searched there with such effort,
You see no essence,
Why do you still, with attachment,
Guard this body?
translation: You look so hard, but you find no essence. Why do you still protect this body with clinging?

academic_translation:
Impurity is not fit for you to eat,
Blood, too, is not fit to drink,
And entrails are not fit to suck, so
What will the body do for you?
translation: Filth is not fit for you to eat. Blood is not fit to drink. Guts are not fit to suck. So what will this body do for you?

academic_translation:
At best, it is fit to be guarded
As food for foxes and vultures.
Every human body
Is merely to be put to use.
translation: At best, it is only guarded as food for foxes and vultures. Every human body is just something to be put to use.

academic_translation:
Even if you guard it in this way,
If the merciless Lord of Death
Snatches it and gives it to birds and dogs,
What can you do at that time?
translation: You might guard it carefully. But the cruel Lord of Death will snatch it away. He will give it to birds and dogs. What can you do then?

academic_translation:
If one does not give clothes and such
Even to a servant who cannot be put to work,
And if this body departs even when nourished,
Why do you exhaust yourself nourishing it?
translation: You would not give clothes to a servant who cannot work. This body will leave you even if you feed it well. Why wear yourself out taking care of it?

academic_translation:
Having given wages to this,
Now make it serve your own purpose.
Without any benefit, to this
Do not give everything.
translation: I pay my body what it needs, like a worker. Then I make it work for my goals. I should not give it everything if it brings no benefit.

academic_translation:
As a mere support for going and coming,
Conceive of the body as a boat, and
In order to accomplish the welfare of sentient beings,
Transform it into a wish-fulfilling body.
translation: I think of my body as just a boat for moving around. To help living beings, I will turn it into a wish-granting body.

academic_translation:
Thus, assume self-mastery, and
Always maintain a smiling face.
Completely abandon frowning and scowling;
Be a friend to wandering beings and speak sincerely.
translation: So, work on being in control of oneself. Always keep a smiling face. Stop frowning and scowling completely. Be a friend to wandering beings and speak honestly.

academic_translation:
Chairs and so forth, recklessly,
Do not throw down with noise.
Also, do not open doors forcefully;
Always delight in acting quietly.
translation: I will not recklessly throw down chairs and other things with noise. I will not open doors with force. I will always enjoy acting quietly.

academic_translation:
Herons, cats, and thieves,
By going silently and stealthily,
Accomplish their desired goals;
The Sage should always act in that manner.
translation: Herons, cats, and thieves get what they want by moving silently and secretly. The Sage should always act in that same way.

academic_translation:
The words of those skilled in advising others,
And words that act beneficially unasked,
Accept them with respect upon your crown;
Always become the disciple of everyone.
translation: Some people give good advice, and others say helpful things without being asked. I will accept their words with respect, placing them on my head like a crown. I will always be a student to everyone.

academic_translation:
To all that is well spoken,
One should say, "Excellently spoken!"
If one sees someone creating merit,
One should generate joy well by praising them.
translation: When someone says something good, I should tell them they spoke well! If I see someone building a store of goodness, I should happily praise them.

academic_translation:
One should speak of good qualities in their absence,
And if good qualities are spoken of, join in.
If one's own good qualities are spoken of,
One should understand that as them knowing good qualities.
translation: I should talk about people's good qualities when they are not around. If others talk about a good quality, I should join in. If they talk about my own good qualities, I should just know they recognize a good quality.

academic_translation:
All undertakings are for the sake of joy,
Which is rare even if bought with a price.
Therefore, through the good qualities achieved by others,
I should enjoy the happiness of joy.
translation: Everything we do is to find joy. True joy is rare even if you try to buy it. So, I should enjoy the happiness of joy by looking at the good qualities others have gained.

academic_translation:
In this life there is no loss for me,
And in the next life there is great happiness.
Through faults, there is unhappiness and suffering,
And in the next life there is great suffering.
translation: I lose nothing in this life, and I will have great happiness in the next. Through faults, there is sadness and suffering now. In the next life, there is great suffering.

academic_translation:
When speaking, one's words should be comforting and coherent,
Clear in meaning and pleasing;
Having abandoned attachment and hatred,
One should speak gently and in moderation.
translation: When I speak, my words should make sense and bring comfort. My meaning should be clear and pleasing. I must let go of clinging and hatred. I should speak gently and not say too much.

academic_translation:
Even when looking at sentient beings with one's eyes,
Thinking, "By relying upon these very beings,
I will become a Buddha,"
One should look in a direct and loving manner.
translation: When I look at living beings, I should think, "By relying on these very beings, I will become a Buddha." I should always look at them in a direct and loving way.

academic_translation:
Whether motivated by constant, intense, fixed aspiration,
Or motivated by an antidote,
Toward the fields of good qualities and benefactors,
And those who are suffering, virtue becomes great.
translation: A good deed becomes very great when you do it with a strong, lasting wish, or as a remedy. This is true when you act toward people with good qualities, people who help you, and those in suffering.

academic_translation:
Having become skilled and endowed with faith,
I shall always perform actions myself.
In all actions, upon anyone at all,
I should not rely.
translation: I will become skilled and full of faith. I will always do my work myself. I should not rely on anyone else for any action at all.

academic_translation:
One should practice the perfection of generosity and the rest
In a progressively more exalted manner.
One should not forsake the greater for the sake of the lesser;
Principally, one should consider the welfare of others.
translation: I should practice the perfection of giving and the other practices better and better over time. I should not give up something big for something small. Above all, I must think about the good of others.

academic_translation:
Having understood this, one should always remain
Diligent in the welfare of others.
Because the Compassionate One sees far ahead,
He permits even prohibited acts for that one.
translation: Knowing this, I must always work hard for the good of others. The Compassionate One sees far ahead. Because of this, he allows a person working for others to do even forbidden things.

academic_translation:
One should share with those fallen into wretched states, the unprotected,
And those established in ascetic discipline;
One should eat only a moderate amount,
And give away everything except the three Dharma robes.
translation: I should share with people in miserable states, people with no protection, and those doing strict practice. I should eat only the right amount. I must give away everything except my three monk's robes.

academic_translation:
This body, which practices the sublime Dharma,
Should not be harmed for the sake of something trivial.
If one acts in this way, the wishes
Of sentient beings will be swiftly fulfilled.
translation: My body practices the holy teachings. I should not harm it for something small. If I act like this, I will quickly fulfill the wishes of every living being.

academic_translation:
While the intention of compassion is impure,
One should not give away this body;
Rather, only when in this and other lives
It becomes a cause for accomplishing a great purpose, should it be given.
translation: If my compassion is not pure, I should not give away my body. I should only give it away if it will help achieve a great purpose in this life and future lives.

academic_translation:
One should not teach the Dharma to the disrespectful,
Nor to those who wear head-wraps while not ill,
Nor to those holding parasols, staffs, or weapons,
Nor to those whose heads are covered.
translation: I should not share the teachings with disrespectful people. I should not teach people who wrap their heads unless they are sick. I must not teach anyone holding an umbrella, a stick, or a weapon, or those with covered heads.

academic_translation:
Do not teach the profound and vast to those of lesser capacity,
Nor to a woman without a man present;
Toward the lesser and supreme Dharmas,
One should always act with equal respect.
translation: I should not share deep and vast teachings with people who are not ready. I should not teach a woman when no man is present. I must always show equal respect to both simple and highest teachings.

academic_translation:
Those who have become vessels for the vast Dharma
Should not be engaged in the lesser Dharma;
Conduct should not be completely forsaken,
Nor should one lure them with sūtras and mantras.
translation: People who are ready for the vast teachings should not practice the lesser teachings instead. Good behavior should not be given up completely. I should not trick people with teaching texts and sacred words.

academic_translation:
Tooth-sticks and saliva,
When discarded, should be covered;
Also, discharging urine and the like
Into usable water or land is deprecated.
translation: When I spit or throw away sticks used to clean teeth, I should cover them up. It is wrong to pee or leave waste in water or on land that people use.
